name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with low volatility (32%), a 4.5% free-cash-flow yield and steady growth; it is ahead of the ETF since purchase.
targets.risks: Only 3.5% above its 200-day average after a 9% weekly drop; the GAAP P/E is distorted by one-off charges.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: The leading US steelmaker behind tariff protection: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 15 and a solid balance sheet; still above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Cyclical demand risk if the correction becomes a growth scare.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes; the steadiest energy name, ahead of the ETF since purchase.
targets.risks: Net debt is 32% of market value, and lower oil prices could slow Permian drilling.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or management cuts its volume guidance.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: The leading cybersecurity platform, with 24% revenue growth and recurring revenue; still 19% above its 200-day average despite the tech selloff.
targets.risks: 80% volatility, and a high valuation going into results confirmed for December 1.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or the December 1 results show annual recurring revenue growth slowing sharply.

targets.name: Hasbro
targets.thesis: Growing (+19% revenue), profitable (18% margin), a 7.8% free-cash-flow yield at a P/E of about 17, and the steadiest share I hold (25% volatility).
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 19% above), or Q4 results show the digital gaming segment slowing sharply.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: The slimmer post-breakup DuPont is being re-rated: up 7.9% over a month in a falling market, with a 4.1% free-cash-flow yield; it is 22 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
targets.risks: Industrial demand could weaken if the selloff turns into a growth scare.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 4% above), or its lead over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: My only refiner: P/E of 7.2, 21% free-cash-flow yield and heavy buybacks, still 19.5% above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Refining margins are volatile, and the share is down 20% over a month.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.4% free-cash-flow yield; up 6.4% over a month in a falling market, 17 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
targets.risks: High leverage (net debt 51% of market value).
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or debt reduction stalls.

targets.name: Target Corporation
targets.thesis: Q3 (reported November 18) beat estimates: sales +7.1%, comparable sales +5.6%, traffic +5%, and full-year guidance raised. The share is 2% under its high and rose in a week when the index fell 7.7%, and it fills my zero staples weight at a P/E of 17.
targets.risks: About $0.50 of the Q3 EPS came from one-off tariff refunds, and a 90% 12-month run leaves room for profit-taking.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 20% above), or holiday sales trends reverse the raised guidance.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Record fiscal Q4 on November 19 (revenue $1.99bn, +41%; orders +53%; above the top of guidance) confirms strong AI and networking test demand; the share's drop looks like market selling, not a business problem.
targets.risks: The share is 19% below its 200-day average and no fiscal 2027 guidance was confirmed, so the downtrend could continue.
targets.exit_if: It falls more than 25% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 20 points since purchase, or a fiscal 2027 outlook implies growth below 10%.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth-management fees plus a dealmaking recovery: 16% revenue growth, a 25.5% margin and a P/E of 13; my only financials holding against a 13% index weight.
targets.risks: It is 14.8% below its 200-day average, right at my exit line, and dealmaking suffers in selloffs.
targets.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Data storage tied to AI demand, at a P/E of 22 with a 5.3% free-cash-flow yield and net cash; held into results on December 1.
targets.risks: It is only 0.5% above its 200-day average with hardware peers falling hard.
targets.exit_if: Q2 results or guidance disappoint, or it closes clearly below its 200-day average (more than 3% under).

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Q3 beat with raised guidance, a 20% margin and net cash; still 6% above its 200-day average after a sharp pullback.
targets.risks: High volatility (79%) and momentum that has rolled over.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

targets.name: Omnicom Group
targets.thesis: Organic growth accelerated to 7.2% in Q3 as the Interpublic merger integration nears completion, with $900 million in targeted synergies. It has a 12% free-cash-flow yield, net cash, trades 4% under its high, and gives the portfolio its first communication-services exposure.
targets.risks: Some of the Q3 lift came from the World Cup and midterm elections, and advertising budgets get cut in a downturn; the GAAP margin is depressed by merger charges.
targets.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 8% above), or organic growth falls back below 3%.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
